text:
oncall-bot: Pager: elevated streaming errors + queue growth in eu-west hosted pool (ALERT: STREAM-EU-1798888000). See alert: https://ops.redwood.internal/alerts/STREAM-EU-1798888000

Morgan L: i'm taking it. oncall -> Morgan L. quick summary from logs: increased queue length on frontends, a handful of workers killing and 502s for streaming lanes. non-stream routes mostly ok.

Ethan P: I see a misconfigured rate-limit rollout that went live an hour ago for fastgen customers. The new policy accidentally removed a per-tenant cap, causing some tenants to burst into the shared pool.

Ops - Riya: runtime metrics corroborate kv-cache pressure and GC spikes. sample logs:
```
2026-03-12T11:02:12Z runtime: kv_cache_util=93% evictions=118
2026-03-12T11:02:13Z worker: pid=3119 exit SIGKILL
2026-03-12T11:02:14Z proxy: 502 upstream closed for req=7b9f
```

Morgan L: okay, immediate plan: 1) re-enable per-tenant caps, 2) bump burst capacity to dedicated fallback for noisy tenants, 3) reduce stream batch_window from 200->100 in eu-west. I'll execute 1 and 3.

Ethan P: re-enabling caps now. I'll also add a short-term ACL to throttle background indexers. Doing it now.

Customer Success - Ben: which customers are noisy? we should flag them for outreach after stabilization.

Ethan P: noisy tenants list: c-314, c-662, c-877. c-314 is an enterprise search customer; c-662 is PLG. We'll do targeted messages once stable.

Support - Hana: already getting tickets saying "stream resets mid-response". i'll prepare a brief initial customer line.

Morgan L: mitigation applied: caps re-enabled + batch_window reduced. early signal: 502 rate down from 4.8% -> 1.5% in 90s. queue length reducing.

Ethan P: applied short ACL for background indexers. watch metrics for 5m then we can post initial status.

Morgan L: draft internal note (ops/product template) below for review:

"Internal incident summary:
- Impact: Partial degradation of streaming responses in eu-west; intermittent 502s and elevated tail latency.
- Root cause (initial): Rate-limit rollout removed per-tenant cap causing bursty traffic into shared pool and triggering kv-cache churn.
- Mitigations applied: Re-enabled per-tenant caps, throttled internal indexers, reduced streaming batch window, moved a subset of noisy tenants to burst fallback.
- Customer impact: Some customers experienced stalled streams and errors; no data loss.
- Next steps: monitor stability for 30m, prepare rollback of the rate-limit change across control plane if bursts continue, schedule follow-up with product for rollout fixes.
- Owners: Morgan L, Ethan P, Riya
"

Ethan P: edit: change 'noisy tenants' to 'identified tenants' and add next update ETA 20 minutes.

Customer Success - Ben: suggested customer-facing line (concise):
"We are investigating intermittent streaming failures and increased latency for requests in the eu-west region. Engineers have applied mitigations and are monitoring. We'll provide an update within 20 minutes."

Support - Hana: i'll use that to reach out to the enterprise tenant c-314 and the PLG customer c-662 once statuspage is live. tagging legal if they ask about data exposure (none).

Morgan L: publishing initial update to statuspage now. @Statuspage Bot please post:
- component: Streaming API (eu-west)
- status: Partial Degradation
- message: We are experiencing intermittent streaming failures and increased latency in eu-west. Mitigations are in place and investigation is ongoing.

Statuspage Bot: Initial update posted (incident id: INC-20260312-XX). Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260312-XX

(oncall-bot): Reminder: follow-up update due in ~18 minutes. Use /incident update to publish.

Morgan L: +12m check: error rate down to 0.9%, p95 latency improving but long-context sessions still slow for one tenant. we'll watch for 30m.

Ethan P: running a canary rollback of the rate-limit rollout for control plane and will monitor routing. If eviction events come down we can plan a full rollback.

Riya: adding traces and eviction logs to incident tracker. recommending a post-incident task to add schema-level limits so that future rollouts don't remove caps silently.

Customer Success - Ben: drafted 20-minute public update: "Update: Error rates have decreased after mitigations; a small number of customers may still experience intermittent failures. Engineers continue to monitor and will provide another update within 60 minutes."

Statuspage Bot: Published update: "Mitigations reducing errors; monitoring continues. Next update within 60 minutes."

Morgan L: canary rollback shows drop in evictions on canary cluster. rolling change back across eu-west slowly.

Support - Hana: customers starting to report restoration. i'll mark tickets pending confirmation and follow up with c-314 and c-662.

(oncall-bot): Reminder: prepare resolved notice when metrics stable for 25m.

Morgan L: metrics stable <0.4% 5xx for 25m, p95 near baseline. drafting resolved message:

"Resolved: The streaming failures and elevated latency in the eu-west region have been resolved. A recent rate-limit rollout accidentally removed per-tenant caps; engineers reverted the change and applied temporary throttles to noisy workloads. Services have returned to normal. A post-incident report will be published with root-cause details and follow-up actions. Contact support if you continue to see issues"

Statuspage Bot: Published resolved update (incident id: INC-20260312-XX, status: Resolved).

Customer Success - Ben: reaching out to impacted customers with a tailored note and offering post-incident review for the enterprise tenant.

Morgan L: filing RCA ticket and scheduling a follow-up to add rollout safety checks in control plane. incident closed. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
